title: Conversion Markup Retained Where a Package Was Charged in Another Currency
content:
**Why is anything retained at all?** Because the markup was paid over on the way in and is not recoverable on the way out. On a cancelled package of Wanderlane's Vacation Package Products, what the deposit and instalment lines were presented to the party in decides how much of the product's conversion markup is retained.

**Every payment in another currency.** Where every deposit and instalment taken on the package was presented to the party in a currency other than the operator's own, the product's conversion markup on what is returned is retained.

**Some, but not all.** Where some but not all of the deposits and instalments taken on the package were presented in a currency other than the operator's own, one half of that markup on what is returned is retained — 50 per cent of it.

**Otherwise.** Where every deposit and instalment taken was presented in the operator's own currency, and where no deposit or instalment has been taken at all, nothing is retained under this note.

## What the lines are counted against

The lines counted are the deposit lines and the instalment lines standing on the package ledger, and each is read against the currency it was presented to the party in. The operator's own currency is the US dollar.

| Deposit and instalment lines presented in another currency | What is retained |
| --- | --- |
| all of them | the product's conversion markup on what is returned |
| some but not all | one half of that markup on what is returned |
| none of them, or no such line at all | nothing |

## Worked on hypothetical particulars

Where the figure reached before any retention is 3,000.00 USD on a product whose conversion markup is 3.0 per cent: with all 4 deposit and instalment lines presented in another currency, 90.00 USD is retained. With 2 of the 4 presented in another currency, one half of that markup is retained, being 45.00 USD. With all 4 presented in the operator's own currency, nothing is retained.
